description: Test of the privilege stages of the ops core (S5a to S5c, features A18 to A20): an administrator account sees the owner's profile, and the profile of each account cached at the PC, and installs a USB device the PC's policy would refuse, only while its session is live and only at the keyboard for a device that needs someone signed in; a step up from a typed session reaches admin. S5b adds cached accounts (an administrator collects the stored hashes of accounts that signed in at a PC, one account joins after a borrowed session), a storage stick accepted at a governed port under an administrator session, and a relayed administrator session. S5c adds a shared local administrator whose hash cracks from a rota fact and signs in on a second PC, a hardened PC that refuses it, and a domain administrator who signs in only on PCs of the domain. Nothing to solve.
test_objective: Prove an ordinary account sees only its own profile, an administrator also sees the owner's, the taskbar marks an administrator session, a keystroke device at the bay socket is refused for a remote session with its own line and accepted at the keyboard under admin, a locked session overrides nothing, a relay session never steps up and a typed session does; a collect needs an administrator session and lists only cached accounts, a borrowed account joins after the borrow, a hash row never holds a password, a governed port takes a stick under an administrator session at its PC, and a relayed administrator may collect while a relayed user may not; a shared local administrator's hash is collected, cracked from a fact and reused on a second PC, a hardened PC refuses it and its own hash does not fall to that fact, and a domain administrator signs in only on the PCs of its domain
